title: Harbor and Postcard Revisited
premise: Elodie Amberdale returns to Saltmere Point for her grandmother's ninetieth birthday, armed with a fake fiancé—Jonah Reyes, a disgraced investigative journalist hiding from the fallout of a story that destroyed an innocent family. What begins as mutual convenience curdles into something real as Jonah realizes the town's beloved harbormaster, Elodie's uncle, was complicit in the cover-up he once investigated. Torn between publishing the truth and protecting the woman who is teaching him to belong, Jonah chooses loyalty over byline—but Elodie, who has spent her life watching people leave, refuses to be anyone's consolation prize. Only when she reads his unpublished manuscript and sees herself in it does she chase him to the last ferry of the season, choosing him not despite his truth but because of it.
about_author: Vesper Marchetti is the pen name of a former maritime archivist who spent a decade cataloguing lighthouse logs along the Atlantic coast before turning to fiction. She writes love stories set in small coastal towns where secrets wash ashore like tide-worn glass.

chapters.title: The Lighthouse Keeps Its Own Counsel
chapters.summary: Elodie's POV. She arrives at Saltmere Point for her grandmother Maren's ninetieth birthday, dreading the inevitable questions about her nonexistent love life. Establishes her habit of fictionalizing her life into safe, past-tense romances. Emotional beat: loneliness disguised as contentment.

chapters.title: A Stranger Buys the Last Scone
chapters.summary: Elodie's POV. At the harbor café she collides with Jonah Reyes, a guarded newcomer reading court documents in the corner booth. They argue over the last scone; sparks of irritation, not attraction—yet. Emotional beat: two people recognizing fellow runaways.

chapters.title: Terms of Engagement
chapters.summary: Alternating POVs. Over cheap wine, they strike a deal: Jonah will pose as Elodie's boyfriend through reunion weekend; she'll rent him her late father's cottage sight unseen. Both conceal their real wounds. Emotional beat: transactional hope with cracks already showing.

chapters.title: Rehearsal Dinner, Unrehearsed Hearts
chapters.summary: Jonah's POV. The fake couple's first performance before the Amberdale clan goes suspiciously well. Uncle Bram, the charismatic harbormaster, welcomes Jonah warmly—and Jonah recognizes his name from old case files. Emotional beat: dread blooming under charm.

chapters.title: What the Tide Brought In
chapters.summary: Elodie's POV. Beach walk with Jonah; she shares the story of her parents' drowning and why she keeps love in past tense. He almost tells her why he really came to Saltmere. Emotional beat: intimacy outpacing the lie.

chapters.title: Ninety Candles, One Wish
chapters.summary: Maren's POV (first time). The birthday party glows with lantern light. Maren, sharp-eyed, privately tells Elodie she knows the engagement is theater—and approves anyway, saying 'fake things can become true if you tend them.' Emotional beat: permission granted.

chapters.title: The Dessert That Undid Them
chapters.summary: Jonah's POV. A stolen moment in the lighthouse kitchen turns into their first real kiss, both pretending afterward it was part of the act. Jonah finds Bram's name again in his notes that night. Emotional beat: desire and suspicion entangled.

chapters.title: Harbormaster's Ledger
chapters.summary: Jonah's POV. He digs into the ferry disaster records at the maritime archive and confirms Bram falsified inspection reports years ago—the same cover-up that cost his last innocent source everything. Emotional beat: justice sharpening into obsession.

chapters.title: Past Tense, Present Danger
chapters.summary: Elodie's POV. She catches Jonah photographing harbor documents and confronts him; he lies badly. Her novelist instincts flag every evasion. Emotional beat: trust fraying at exactly the wrong moment.

chapters.title: Storm Warning
chapters.summary: Alternating POVs. A gale traps them together in the lighthouse overnight; power fails, candles burn, and they make love for the first time. Afterward Jonah nearly confesses. Emotional beat: peak closeness on the edge of betrayal.

chapters.title: The Story He Never Sold
chapters.summary: Jonah's POV. Flashback chapter: the investigation that ruined him—an editor buried his exposé, his source was destroyed, his career ended. Reveals why truth has been his only religion since. Emotional beat: sympathy deepened, stakes clarified.

chapters.title: Bram's Toast
chapters.summary: Elodie's POV. At a harbor festival, Bram gives a rousing speech about safety and stewardship while Jonah watches with barely contained fury. Elodie sees his face and finally understands there is a story—and that she may be inside it. Emotional beat: dread crystallizing.

chapters.title: Interrogation by Firelight
chapters.summary: Alternating POVs. Elodie demands the truth; Jonah admits who he is and what Bram did. She defends her uncle; he accuses her of choosing comfortable lies. They part angry, the fake engagement suspended between them. Emotional beat: first true rupture.

chapters.title: What Grandmother Knew
chapters.summary: Maren's POV. Maren reveals to Elodie that she has known about Bram's falsified reports for years and stayed silent to hold the family together—a confession that reframes loyalty as its own kind of cowardice. Emotional beat: generational mirror.

chapters.title: Deadline: Last Ferry
chapters.summary: Jonah's POV. His former editor offers to run the Bram story if Jonah delivers confirmation within days—the last ferry of the season leaves Saturday. Publishing means destroying Elodie's family; silence means betraying his dead source. Emotional beat: impossible arithmetic.

chapters.title: The Manuscript in the Drawer
chapters.summary: Elodie's POV. Packing Jonah's things, she finds his unpublished novel and reads it through the night—discovering that the villain is drawn from himself, and that she appears in its pages as the person who taught him to see clearly. Emotional beat: understanding arriving too late.

chapters.title: Confession at Low Tide
chapters.summary: Alternating POVs. Jonah tells Bram he knows, giving him until the ferry departs to confess publicly himself. Bram refuses, threatening to paint Jonah as a blackmailer. Elodie overhears everything. Emotional beat: all masks off.

chapters.title: The Family We Choose
chapters.summary: Elodie's POV. She convenes the Ambergdales—no wait, the Amberdales—at the lighthouse and lays out the truth herself, refusing to let either man weaponize her family. Maren backs her. Bram breaks down and agrees to face the maritime board. Emotional beat: Elode seizing authorship of her own story.

chapters.title: Empty Dock
chapters.summary: Jonah's POV. Believing he has lost Elodie after her fury at being managed, Jonah packs and walks to the ferry landing in gray dawn light. He leaves the finished manuscript on her doorstep with a note: 'You were never a chapter. You were the whole book.' Emotional beat: sacrifice mistaken for surrender.

chapters.title: Last Ferry of the Season
chapters.summary: Elodie's POV. She reads the note, then the final pages where he chose her over the byline before she ever asked. She runs the cliff path as the ferry sounds its horn. Emotional beat: desperate, hopeful sprint.

chapters.title: All Aboard the Truth
chapters.summary: Climax. Elodie reaches the dock as the gangway rises; Jonah steps off rather than board without her answer. She tells him she doesn't want the man who abandoned the story or the man who hid it—she wants the one who came back and told it anyway. They kiss as the ferry departs empty. Emotional beat: love chosen in full knowledge.

chapters.title: Postscript, Present Tense
chapters.summary: Epilogue, alternating POVs. Spring: Bram serves his community-service sentence restoring the lighthouse; Maren presides over Sunday dinners; Jonah publishes the full story with Elodie as co-byline. Her new novel opens with two strangers and a scone. Emotional beat: belonging, written in present tense.
